checks.detail: SCA on (lambda=1, literal +log form): min_t Gamma_raw = 2.1813 over 8.0 s, boundary crossings = 0
the constraint is genuinely binding: active on 50% of the steps and the dual multiplier reaches nu_max = 0.001 > 0 (a constraint that never binds would make the safety claim vacuous)

Eq.(26) in the closed loop: max relative error against a central difference of Gamma(f(q)) over 400 configurations = 1.17e-09; +grad_q Gamma raises Gamma on 400/400 configurations (a sign-agnostic FD test would not catch a flipped row)

four event classes counted separately on the SCA-on run: LOG_DOMAIN 0, QP_INFEASIBLE 0, SOLVER_FAILURE 0, BOUNDARY_CROSSING 0.  Why each zero is zero, with the run that exercises the class: LOG_DOMAIN -- the log budget binds while Gamma_raw is still ~2.18, so the trajectory is deflected before the domain ends (exercised by construction in P8.6, which starts inside the domain); QP_INFEASIBLE -- the barrier is satisfied inside the velocity box instead of saturating it (exercised by N8.1: 701 steps, N8.3: 1473 steps, so the counter is wired to a live code path and is not dead); SOLVER_FAILURE -- every solve returns a KKT-verified point, max primal residual 8.3e-16 (never exercised anywhere: the exact enumerator either finds the optimum or proves infeasibility); BOUNDARY_CROSSING -- 0 with SCA on against 656 with SCA off (P8.5), i.e. the counter is proven live by the matched control

matched control with SCA switched off, same task and same initial state: min_t Gamma_raw = -2.3942 and 656 boundary crossings.  Without this the SCA-on result would be indistinguishable from 'the task never approaches the boundary'

PAPER_FALLBACK tested on its own, separately from the literal log form: from a configuration with Gamma_raw = -3.015 the fallback fires (rhs = -1000, i.e. it demands Gamma_dot >= 1000).  The direction is right -- the box vertex along +grad Gamma raises Gamma at 28.2/s (one 1e-6 s step: +2.82e-05) -- but the best achievable rate is 28.2, so the hard-constrained QP is INFEASIBLE: the fallback is a *soft-formulation* device and this fixture shows it cannot be honoured as a hard row

flipping the sign of grad_q Gamma (a one-character defect) drops min_t Gamma_raw from 2.181 to 0.986 and freezes the run at t = 4.495 s instead of completing it: the row's sign is observable in the closed loop

lambda = 0 makes the row Gamma_dot >= 0.  Measured: min_t Gamma_raw stays at 6.380 and the constraint is active on 75% of the steps, so the approach is blocked immediately.  This FALSIFIES the plan's expectation that lambda = 0 should be the looser setting (see the POST report): far from the boundary lambda = 0 removes the log budget rather than adding margin

the printed b3 = -log(Gamma-1) inverts the requested rate: at Gamma_raw = 6.38 it demands Gamma_dot >= +1.68 (a retreat) where the KKT form allows -1.68, and at Gamma_raw = 1.01 it demands -4.61 where the KKT form demands +4.61 -- i.e. the protection vanishes exactly where it is needed.  Closed loop: saturated from t = 0.635 s, min_t Gamma_raw held at 6.380 by the velocity box, not by the boundary

zero-padding defects: a pair gradient of length 3 into 2 columns raises ValueError (dimension assertion), and writing the arm-2 block into the arm-1 columns changes the predicted Gamma_dot by 1.0e+00 relative -- the FD check P8.3 would reject it

no silent clamping on the SCA path: np.clip was replaced by a tripwire and the closed loop ran 60 steps without calling it (the only clip call in the package sits in the unused SLSQP backend).  Gamma_raw outside the log domain is handled by the labelled PAPER_FALLBACK, never by clipping

step size multiplied by 10: min_t Gamma_raw moves from 2.1813 to 2.1645 and the crossing count goes from 0 to 0.  Discretisation error is real -- the hold point is not step-size invariant, so no 'any step size is perfect' claim is made

step-size convergence over dt = ['0.005', '0.0025', '0.00125']: min_t Gamma_raw = ['2.18127', '2.18267', '2.18316'], successive differences <= 1.4e-03 -- the reported minimum is a property of the mechanism, not of dt
